paragraphs: On Thursday, the Explorers made a nature book. Every member wrote one page, and Teacher Kim put the pages together. Lily and May made the contents page in the school library. Lily wrote the titles, and May wrote the page numbers. "I have already written the first three titles," said Lily. "Good," said May. "Now we need to put them in order."

This is the first half of the contents page. "Page two: What Is an Explorer?" "Page three: Leaf Fun. Collect a leaf, and put it on a page with glue." "Page five: The Lost Hat. A short story by Mia." "Page six: A Walk with Ranger Mark." May looked at the list and saw that there was no page four and no page seven. "Where are page four and page seven?" she asked. "Leaf Fun and the walk have two pages each," said Lily. "Then the list is right," said May.

This is the second half of the contents page. "Page eight: The Park Boat. Ranger Mark has a license to drive it." "Page nine: Boys against Girls. The big nature quiz." "Page ten: My Best Experience. A page by Leo." "Page eleven: Our Map of the Park." Lily put a small picture of a leaf next to the quiz title. "Is the quiz about leaves?" asked May. "No, it is about animals and plants," said Lily.

May took the book and read the captions. Under the leaf photo on page three, the caption says "A leaf from the big tree." On page eight, there is a photo of the boat. Its caption says "The boat is in the middle of the lake." The map on page eleven shows the gate, the lake, and the paths. "Leo's page is the only page with no photo," said May. "He drew a cartoon of Ranger Mark instead." "That is a good idea, because Leo loves to draw," said Lily.

Teacher Kim came and read the contents page. "The titles are clear, and the numbers are in order," she said. "One more thing: you need a title for the whole book." "We will call it The Explorers' Nature Book," said May. Lily wrote it at the top of the page and smiled. "Now the book is ready for the school library," said Teacher Kim.
text.summary: Lily and May write the contents page for a nature book of the Explorers club. The list shows the pages, the titles, and a few captions, and the two girls check it with Teacher Kim.

sentences.text: On Thursday, the Explorers made a nature book.
Every member wrote one page, and Teacher Kim put the pages together.
Lily and May made the contents page in the school library.
Lily wrote the titles, and May wrote the page numbers.
"I have already written the first three titles," said Lily.
"Good," said May.
"Now we need to put them in order."
This is the first half of the contents page.
"Page two: What Is an Explorer?"
"Page three: Leaf Fun. Collect a leaf, and put it on a page with glue."
"Page five: The Lost Hat. A short story by Mia."
"Page six: A Walk with Ranger Mark."
May looked at the list and saw that there was no page four and no page seven.
"Where are page four and page seven?" she asked.
"Leaf Fun and the walk have two pages each," said Lily.
"Then the list is right," said May.
This is the second half of the contents page.
"Page eight: The Park Boat. Ranger Mark has a license to drive it."
"Page nine: Boys against Girls. The big nature quiz."
"Page ten: My Best Experience. A page by Leo."
"Page eleven: Our Map of the Park."
Lily put a small picture of a leaf next to the quiz title.
"Is the quiz about leaves?" asked May.
"No, it is about animals and plants," said Lily.
May took the book and read the captions.
Under the leaf photo on page three, the caption says "A leaf from the big tree."
On page eight, there is a photo of the boat.
Its caption says "The boat is in the middle of the lake."
The map on page eleven shows the gate, the lake, and the paths.
"Leo's page is the only page with no photo," said May.
"He drew a cartoon of Ranger Mark instead."
"That is a good idea, because Leo loves to draw," said Lily.
Teacher Kim came and read the contents page.
"The titles are clear, and the numbers are in order," she said.
"One more thing: you need a title for the whole book."
"We will call it The Explorers' Nature Book," said May.
Lily wrote it at the top of the page and smiled.
"Now the book is ready for the school library," said Teacher Kim.
